description: Hand-curated resistance mechanisms for the MVP, not pulled live from CARD or generated by RGI/AMRFinderPlus against an uploaded genome -- that pipeline (Layer 2 as originally scoped) needs strain FASTA input and a local CARD/RGI install, which this MVP does not wire up yet. A strain is defined by picking mechanisms from this fixed reference list (see data/strains/*.json). gene_marker names (blaCTX-M-15, mcr-1, dfrA1, etc.) are real, well-established resistance determinant families from the clinical microbiology literature. `affected_drugs` multipliers are NOT sourced from any specific fold-MIC-change study or live CARD/ARO lookup (this environment has no network access to verify one) -- each mechanism's `magnitude_confidence` field says explicitly what is and isn't backed by literature: the ORDINAL pattern (near-zero for a mechanism's known substrates, ~1.0 for drugs it doesn't touch, partial values for documented partial-protection cases like carbapenems against ESBL) reflects standard, textbook-level clinical microbiology and is high confidence; the exact decimal within each band is an illustrative placeholder, not a citation. An earlier version of this file included specific numeric CARD/ARO accession IDs (e.g. "ARO:3001864") next to each mechanism; those have been removed because they were never checked against a live CARD instance and risked being read as verified citations they were not.

mechanisms.name: CTX-M-15 extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: Ordinal pattern is high confidence and standard clinical microbiology: CTX-M-15 is a well-documented ESBL that hydrolyses penicillins and oxyimino-cephalosporins efficiently (isolates are reliably reported resistant), spares carbapenems almost entirely (meropenem stays clinically active against ESBL producers absent a separate carbapenemase), and is a known substrate for tazobactam's inhibitory activity (giving piperacillin-tazobactam partial protection) -- and ertapenem is well documented to be more vulnerable to ESBL activity than meropenem specifically. The exact decimals (0.03 vs 0.05, 0.35, 0.55, 0.92) are illustrative approximations of that pattern, not fold-MIC values from a specific study.
mechanisms.description: Hydrolyses penicillins and oxyimino-cephalosporins efficiently; spares carbapenems almost entirely, gives ertapenem partial (porin-loss-independent) attenuation, and is partly checked by tazobactam.

mechanisms.name: KPC-2 carbapenemase
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: Ordinal pattern is high confidence: KPC-2 is a well-documented class A serine carbapenemase with broad hydrolytic activity across penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems alike (unlike ESBLs, it does not spare carbapenems) -- this is the defining, guideline-level clinical fact about KPC producers. Exact decimals are illustrative, not literature-derived.
mechanisms.description: Broad-spectrum serine carbapenemase; hydrolyses nearly all beta-lactams in the panel including carbapenems.

mechanisms.name: AcrAB-TolC efflux pump overexpression (marR mutant)
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: The AcrAB-TolC system's broad substrate range (fluoroquinolones, some beta-lactams, nitrofurans) and marR loss-of-function as a well-known constitutive-overexpression route are established literature findings. The partial (not near-zero) multipliers reflect that efflux overexpression alone typically produces moderate, not complete, resistance -- but the specific fold-reduction per drug is illustrative, not measured.
mechanisms.description: Constitutive overexpression of the AcrAB-TolC efflux system lowers effective intracellular concentration across a broad range of substrate classes. Multiplier scales the drug's effective inhibition strength down (0.4 = effective strength reduced to 40% of nominal).

mechanisms.name: GyrA S83L target-site mutation
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: GyrA S83L is the single most-reported fluoroquinolone-resistance-conferring quinolone-resistance-determining-region (QRDR) mutation in E. coli in the literature; that it substantially raises MICs is high confidence. The exact multiplier is illustrative and, because DNA gyrase is absent from this metabolic reconstruction, has no effect on any FBA computation regardless -- it only feeds the reasoning layer's qualitative confidence labeling.
mechanisms.description: Reduces fluoroquinolone binding affinity at the GyrA quinolone-resistance-determining region. Not FBA-simulable (DNA gyrase absent from the metabolic reconstruction); factored into the confidence/reasoning layer only, not into growth predictions.

mechanisms.name: DfrA1 trimethoprim-insensitive dihydrofolate reductase
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: dfrA gene cassettes conferring trimethoprim-insensitive DHFR are a well-established, textbook target-bypass resistance mechanism (frequently plasmid/integron-borne); that they produce near-complete loss of trimethoprim activity is high confidence. Exact decimal is illustrative.
mechanisms.description: Plasmid-borne DHFR variant with drastically reduced trimethoprim affinity; effectively bypasses target inhibition at clinical concentrations.

mechanisms.name: Sul1 sulfonamide-insensitive dihydropteroate synthase
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: sul1/sul2 target-bypass DHPS variants are a well-established sulfonamide resistance mechanism, commonly co-carried with dfrA cassettes on the same integron. Near-complete activity loss is high confidence; exact decimal is illustrative.
mechanisms.description: Alternative DHPS with low sulfonamide affinity, target-bypass resistance mechanism.

mechanisms.name: MCR-1 phosphoethanolamine transferase (colistin resistance)
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: MCR-1 (plasmid-mediated colistin resistance via lipid A phosphoethanolamine modification) is a well-documented, clinically important mechanism first reported in 2015 and since found worldwide. That it typically produces moderate (not complete) MIC elevation relative to the near-total loss seen with enzymatic drug-inactivating mechanisms is a reasonable qualitative distinction; the exact multiplier is illustrative.
mechanisms.description: Adds phosphoethanolamine to lipid A, reducing the negative charge colistin binds to. Represented as a reduction in colistin's effective strength rather than a lipid-A-pathway reaction change, since the modification is a chemical decoy, not a metabolic block.

mechanisms.name: ArmA 16S rRNA methyltransferase (pan-aminoglycoside resistance)
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: 16S rRNA methyltransferases (ArmA, RmtB, and related) conferring high-level pan-aminoglycoside resistance (including amikacin, often considered a last-resort aminoglycoside) are well documented. Near-complete activity loss across the whole class is high confidence; exact decimal is illustrative and, since the ribosome is absent from this reconstruction, has no effect on FBA computation -- reasoning-layer-only.
mechanisms.description: Methylates the 16S rRNA decoding site, blocking aminoglycoside binding across the class. Not FBA-simulable (ribosome absent from the reconstruction); factored into the reasoning layer's confidence scoring only.

mechanisms.name: FosA fosfomycin-inactivating glutathione transferase
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: FosA (glutathione S-transferase family fosfomycin-modifying enzyme) is a well-documented, often chromosomally-encoded fosfomycin resistance determinant in Enterobacterales, notably K. pneumoniae. It is frequently under-expressed unless induced or overexpressed via regulatory mutation, so real-world effect size varies considerably by isolate; this MVP models it as a simple binary near-complete-inactivation determinant rather than capturing that expression-level variability. Exact decimal is illustrative.
mechanisms.description: Conjugates glutathione to fosfomycin, inactivating it before it reaches MurA. Chromosomal in many Enterobacterales, often under-expressed unless induced -- represented here as a simple binary resistance determinant for MVP simplicity.

mechanisms.name: NfsA/NfsB nitroreductase loss-of-function
mechanisms.magnitude_confidence: Loss-of-function mutations in nfsA (and to a lesser extent nfsB) as the primary chromosomal route to nitrofurantoin resistance are well established in the literature. Not FBA-simulable (see the nitrofurantoin panel entry: nfsB is present in this model's gene set but only via an unrelated moonlighting reaction, and no nitrofuran-activation chemistry exists in the reconstruction at all); reasoning-layer-only effect.
mechanisms.description: Prevents prodrug activation of nitrofurantoin. Not FBA-simulable (activation chemistry outside metabolic reconstruction); reasoning-layer-only effect.
